label: original-phase steps 3-6 after >=2 earlier inputs from {0,y,b,q,l}
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase: 98.8% of mass, peak at t=4-5, essentially nothing at t<=2 or t>=8, a small amount at the <DEL> step, and none in the copy phase. Position alone (phase 0, t in 3..6) covers 96% of activations but has only 4% precision. Whether it fires depends on which tokens came earlier: rates rise sharply when prev_tok/prev2_tok is 0, y, b, q or l (4-7x lift), and with more digits in the sequence. Requiring >=2 earlier inputs from {0,y,b,q,l} gives dev P=0.20, R=0.71, mass recall 0.79, and the coverage it gets is higher for the larger activations. It looks like a graded, token-weighted accumulation over the prefix gated by position, and a boolean predicate captures it only approximately. Current tokens 0, w, 1, y add to it too. It does not fire in the copy phase or at steps 0-1.
